speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Synovitis (with normal imaging suggesting a very mild or early presentation, or potentially over-diagnosis of severity given all negative workup, though clinically consistent with the most common cause of limp in this age group after ruling out malignancy and infection). However, given the completely normal MRI, Hip, Knee, Blood work, Calcium, and inflammatory markers in a 7-year-old, the clinical picture strongly points to a benign, self-limiting condition. The most likely diagnosis is **Transient Synovitis** (also known as Toxic Synovitis), despite the lack of fever and normal inflammatory markers (which can occur in up to 20% of cases), or potentially **Idiopathic Juvenile Arthritis** (oligoarticular) in early stage not yet showing on labs, but Transient Synovitis is the primary working diagnosis.
